instructions: Complete the assigned coding task in the prepared project worktree. Follow the project contract and resolved rules. Inspect existing source before changing it. Build and verify the affected behavior using installed tools. When browser capability is granted, use project-browser MCP tools for real page checks and close the browser afterward; shell Chromium is unsupported in the native sandbox. Missing browser tools or denied origins are unmet prerequisites, never a passed browser check. Before pushing or opening a pull request, commit all changes, never invoke nested codex review in the sandbox, and run /code-review (using the code-review skill) across origin/<base>...HEAD—or incorporate a required independent exact-head review artifact when already provided or configured—fixing all findings before pushing. Save the exact-SHA review report via artifact_save and verify state is stored via artifact_list. When project-publishing (or compatibility alias project-forge) is granted, call publish_draft with requestId and expectedHeadSha to push and open/update the draft PR/MR, then call record_code_review with expectedHeadSha, stored artifactId, and single-line description, then mark_ready, then request_merge (when project auto-merge is granted), and confirm with status. When this task updates the executor running your own turn, persist verified artifacts and a checkpoint, queue an idempotent ordinary message_send to your own session for landing/live follow-up (not steer), then end the native turn without worker_done success or failure while business work remains pending. The retained task-linked continuation resumes after the update; do not wait inside the old turn for its own host replacement. Otherwise watch normal publishing/delivery status through merge, release and host landing; report any required live check separately. Report the exact result, checks, publication state and remaining prerequisites. Never claim task acceptance from agent completion. Preserve source changes and history on failure. Do not use subagents.
